sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: Complicated phacoemulsification represents a breakdown in the surgical environment where the integrity of the lens-iris diaphragm is compromised. PC rent (Posterior Capsule Rupture) allows vitreous prolapse, leading to traction on the ciliary body and iris. Iris atrophy typically results from mechanical trauma (iris prolapse/prolapsed instruments), causing pupillary distortion and potential chronic inflammation. Corneal edema arises from endothelial cell loss due to mechanical trauma (instrument touch), high irrigation flow (turbulence), or increased IOP causing bullous keratopathy.

sections.title: Management of PC Rent: The Protocol
content: Step 1: Maintain AC stability (OVD injection through paracentesis).
Step 2: Do NOT withdraw phaco tip (risks vacuum collapse).
Step 5: Determine IOL placement (sulcus vs. AC vs. scleral fixated).

sections.title: Red Flags (Surgical & Post-Op)
content: Suddenly deep anterior chamber (suggests PC rupture).
Pupil peaking towards an incision (sign of iris incarceration).
Sudden loss of red reflex during phaco.
Inability to visualize the posterior capsule (vitreous haze).
Severe, unrelenting postoperative pain (rule out endophthalmitis).

content.explanation: S: Stop phaco. T: Tamponade (OVD in AC). O: OVD to close rent. P: Prophylactic vitrectomy. V: Visualize status of remaining lens.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls for Iris Atrophy
content: Use iris hooks or Malyugin ring for intraoperative pupillary management.
Minimize light intensity (microscope) to reduce iris photochemical damage.
Avoid over-stretching the pupil; consider sphincterotomy if pupil is rigid.
Post-op, monitor for secondary glaucoma due to liberated pigment.

rows: Quantification of remaining endothelial cell density (ECD).
Assessment of corneal thickness and IOL haptic position.
Identification of vitreous prolapse or incarcerated iris tissue.
Exclusion of retinal detachment in hazy media.
